title: Duplicate styles.json id refused so dry run matches run
Rail scope pass silently drops a row whose vids is not a blob
body:
## Summary
counts.ts fromScope skips any scope row whose `vids` is not a Uint8Array with `continue`, so a corrupt row vanishes from the match and its facet counts with no error and no count.

## Description
packages/kernel/src/library/counts.ts:124 (`if (!(blob instanceof Uint8Array)) continue;`). The data-access golden path's honesty contract (software-engineering/backend-platform/data-layer/data-access, 'The honesty contract: when a row is corrupt') allows a collection read to fail whole or degrade VISIBLY, and bans the silent skip. Today the bare rail (library_counts, trigger-kept) still counts the row while the filtered page omits it, so the two disagree with nothing said. Fixed looks like either arm: (a) throw AppError('internal', 'library row <seq>: vids is not a blob') - the page fails whole; (b) count the skipped rows and surface them on LibraryPage (a @gt/domain/library type change, outside this context).

## Flow
- UPDATE library_items SET vids = 'corrupt' for one of two 'calm' takes
- queryLibrary({kind:'audio', facets:{mood:['calm']}})
- observed: total 1, ids [b]; bare rail says calm = 2; no error

## Expected impact
An operator filtering the Library sees one item fewer than the rail promised, silently. Arm (a) could brick the page on a single corrupt row; arm (b) widens a domain type.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a corrupt index row is never silently dropped
Before: probe 2026-10-24: rail calm=2, filtered total=1, ids [b], no error
After: arm (a): queryLibrary returns err internal naming the seq; arm (b): total 1 + skipped 1 on the page
Method: probe - Before measured on a seeded corrupt row; the After needs a choice between arms, one of which edits @gt/domain/library (out of scope)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: packages/kernel/test/library.test.ts case: corrupt one item's vids via raw UPDATE, assert queryLibrary(filtered) either errs naming the seq (arm a) or reports skipped=1 (arm b); seed red on HEAD (total 1, no error)

title: pruneFeed leaves every library_values row it orphaned
body:
## Summary
pruneFeed deletes items (facets cascade) but never the library_values rows no item references any more, so the vocabulary table only grows.

## Description
packages/kernel/src/library/write.ts pruneFeed deletes library_fts and library_items rows; library_values (schema.ts library_values) has no foreign key and no sweep. valuesOf (counts.ts) loads every value of the rail's groups on every query, and `key:value` search (clauses.ts) resolves against it, so orphans cost memory per query and resolve searches to values no item holds (harmless zero results). Fixed: after the prune, delete values with no library_facets row and that are not a current item column value (kind/state/origin/source), inside the same transaction - vids reference only live values, so no packed id dangles.

## Flow
- upsert 3 takes (10 values)
- pruneFeed(feed, keep = {})
- observed: 0 items, 10 library_values rows

## Expected impact
Store size and per-query valuesOf cost stop growing with vocabulary churn; a missed live value would drop a rail label (falls back to the raw value).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - library_values holds only values some item carries
Before: probe 2026-10-24: 10 values before prune, 10 after, 0 items
After: predicted 0 values after pruning every item; same 50k probe timings for queryLibrary
Method: probe - Before measured; After not built: the prune's cost at 50k (lib/library/probe.ts) is the second figure the change needs
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: probe: {v0: 10, v1: 10, items: 0} after pruneFeed(s, 'f', new Set())
instrument: library.test.ts case counting library_values after a full prune (seed red: 10 -> 10), plus lib/library/probe.ts prune timing at 50k on both arms
